rules.statement: Don't let an infrastructure change destroy or replace a stateful resource as an incidental side effect: use a `moved` block, a gated adoption path, or a recorded decision.
rules.why: Live roots manage real production infrastructure, and a merge applies to production after approval. An unplanned `-/+` on a stateful resource loses data.
rules.check: Look for renamed or re-addressed resources, or changed force-new arguments, on stateful resources (databases, buckets, KMS keys, state stores) that have no `moved` block, no gated adoption, and no ADR reference.

rules.statement: Pin every third-party GitHub Action by its full commit SHA, with the version tag in a trailing comment.
rules.why: Tags can be moved, so pinning by SHA is the secure default for CI supply-chain integrity. The comment keeps the version readable.
rules.check: In workflow `uses:` lines, flag references pinned to a tag or branch (`@v4`, `@main`) or to a short SHA, and full-SHA pins that lack a `# vX.Y.Z` comment.

rules.statement: Have CI authenticate to the cloud through short-lived OIDC federation, never through stored long-lived credentials or access keys.
rules.why: Short-lived federated credentials are the modern, secure default. Stored secrets can leak and never expire.
rules.check: Flag workflows or infrastructure that add static cloud access keys, secret-stored credentials, or IAM users with access keys for CI, where an OIDC role assumption could be used instead.

rules.statement: Scope IAM roles and policies to least privilege for a single root and a single environment.
rules.why: Least-privilege IAM limits what one compromised role or pipeline can reach.
rules.check: Flag IAM policies with wildcard actions or resources, and roles shared across environments or roots.

rules.statement: Use customer-managed KMS keys wherever the platform must control the key, enforce encryption on state and plan storage, and turn deletion protection on by default.
rules.why: These are the secure infrastructure defaults the platform adopts without asking.
rules.check: Flag new storage, state, or plan resources that use provider-managed keys where control is needed, that lack enforced encryption, or that have deletion protection off or defaulted to false.

rules.statement: Never commit a credential, token, state file, plan or apply output, or backup to the repository.
rules.why: The repository is public on purpose, so anything committed is published.
rules.check: Look for `*.tfstate`, plan files, pasted plan or apply output, backups, keys, or tokens added in the diff, including inside docs or PR text.

rules.statement: Make a breaking component change (an interface change or a forced resource replacement) as an explicit breaking release marked `!`, rather than adding a compatibility shim.
rules.why: Pre-1.0 greenfield code defaults to the best long-term, cohesive design over compatibility-preserving patches.
rules.check: Flag compatibility shims, deprecated aliases, or duplicate inputs added only to avoid a break, and breaking interface changes whose PR title lacks `!`.

rules.statement: When a change corrects an insecure or outdated shape, update the surrounding comments and docs that describe it in the same change.
rules.why: Existing comments and docs are point-in-time artifacts. Leaving them stale keeps teaching the wrong shape.
rules.check: Look for a corrected implementation whose nearby comments, README, or docs still describe the old behavior.

rules.statement: Never add agent attribution to a commit or pull request: no `Co-authored-by:` trailer naming an agent or bot, no `Claude-Session:` trailer, and no 'Generated with' line.
rules.why: A commit records the people who authored it. A squash merge carries the trailers onto `main`, and removing them there means rewriting published history.
rules.check: Inspect commit messages and the PR body for agent co-author trailers, session trailers, or 'Generated with' lines.

rules.statement: Title a pull request as a conventional commit, `type(scope)!: summary`, and give it a body with Why, Changes, and Verified sections, ending with a `Closes` or `Refs` issue reference when it serves an issue.
rules.why: Pull requests are squash-merged, so the title becomes the commit subject and the body becomes the commit message.
rules.check: Check that the PR title follows the conventional-commit format with a scope, and that the body has Why, Changes, and Verified sections plus a trailing `Closes`/`Refs` line when an issue applies.

rules.statement: For a pull request that changes live infrastructure roots, state the expected deploy plan summary (`N to add, N to change, N to destroy`) in the body.
rules.why: Merging applies to production after approval, so reviewers need the expected impact up front.
rules.check: For PRs touching live roots, check that the body states the expected add/change/destroy counts.

rules.statement: Don't change a reusable infrastructure module and a live root's reference to it in the same pull request: release the module first, then bump the root's `?ref=` to the release tag in a separate pull request.
rules.why: A component change reaches live roots only through a tagged release, which keeps what is deployed traceable to a permanent version.
rules.check: Flag PRs that modify both module sources and live roots, and live-root module sources that point to a branch or untagged ref instead of a `vX.Y.Z` tag.

rules.statement: Never commit an agent's working plan file (`PLAN.md`) to the repository.
rules.why: The plan file is untracked working state and must never reach `main`. Its lasting decisions and lessons are promoted to durable docs instead.
rules.check: Flag a diff that adds or modifies `PLAN.md`.
